items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: it was Bud that I met when I was about 15½. It was that next two-, three-year period that I was around Bud a lot that I really absorbed a lot of understanding about the music, just being in his presence.

ctx.x: No. We gave him an honorary doctorate at the Hartt School, the University of Hartford. I was with him that whole day. That was a great afternoon that I spent with him. And one time in Austria, I went up to his room. We were both on this same show. I was with a different – with my band. I went up to his room with him. He was very upset over something that had happened. I don’t want to mention it in the Smithsonian interview. But it was about another musician that wanted Dizzy to be in his video. Dizzy was saying,…

But I think perhaps, when you talk about the ’40s, my mind goes to Bud before anybody, Bud Powell, because it was Bud that I met when I was about 15½. It was that next two-, three-year period that I was around Bud a lot that I really absorbed a lot of understanding about the music, just being in his presence.
I’m going to come back to Bud Powell too. But just to stay on this . . .
